about.title: Personal Injury Help in Perris, California
about.longDescription: Perris sits where Interstate 215 meets the Ramona Expressway, and plenty of Riverside County traffic passes through on the way to Lake Perris or the freeway. In 2025, the most recent final reporting year, the city recorded 267 injury collisions. Those crashes left 395 people hurt and took 6 lives. Public records show the heaviest collision counts along Perris Boulevard, 4th Street, and the Ramona Expressway, with reports tending to peak on Monday afternoons between 2 p.m. and 4 p.m. Numbers like these are only counts. Behind each one is someone trying to figure out what comes next after a wreck, a fall, or a bite. That is where LawProactive comes in. We are a free service, not a law firm. Our role is simple: listen to what happened, then connect you with an independent personal injury attorney who handles cases in Perris and the surrounding county. The attorneys in our network take injury matters on contingency, which means no fee unless there is a recovery in your case. California gives most injured people two years to bring a claim, but that clock can shrink to six months when a public agency is involved. Reaching out early keeps your choices open.

whyChoose.title: What California Law Means for Your Perris Claim

items.title: Two years for most claims, sometimes less
items.desc: California generally allows two years from the date of injury to file a lawsuit. If a city, county, or state agency is involved, a claim may need to be filed in as little as six months.

items.title: Partial fault does not shut you out
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still recover even if you share some blame. Your recovery is simply reduced by your percentage of fault.

items.title: No cap on pain and suffering in ordinary cases
items.desc: For standard injury claims in California, there is no statutory ceiling on non-economic damages such as pain, emotional distress, or loss of enjoyment of life.

items.title: Contingency fees, so nothing comes out of your pocket up front
items.desc: The independent attorneys in our network handle injury cases on contingency. If there is no recovery, there is no attorney fee.

items.question: Is LawProactive a law firm?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free connection service. We listen to what happened and match you with an independent personal injury attorney who handles cases in Perris and Riverside County. We do not give legal advice or represent you ourselves.

items.question: How long do I have to act after an injury in Perris?
items.answer: For most personal injury claims in California, the deadline is two years from the date of the injury. If your claim involves a government entity, such as a city vehicle or a hazard on public property, you may have only six months to file a claim. Because those windows can close quickly, it helps to speak with an attorney sooner rather than later.

items.question: What if I was partly responsible for the crash?
items.answer: California follows pure comparative fault. That means sharing some of the blame reduces what you can recover but does not prevent you from recovering at all. An attorney can help sort out how fault is likely to be assigned in your situation.

items.question: What will an attorney cost me?
items.answer: Attorneys in the LawProactive network work on a contingency basis. You do not pay a fee unless there is a recovery in your case, and the fee comes out of that recovery rather than your pocket. The initial connection through LawProactive is free as well.
